info.title: payment-api
info.description: The payment HTTP routes and OpenAPI contract over the chain-neutral wallet and index abstractions. Every asset is an open tag; no chain or asset is named in this contract.

get.summary: Read readiness and network health from memory
get.description: Public memory-only readiness. Ready when every network is ready or quarantined and at least one is ready. No RPC or storage reads.
The contract every route is generated from; public, like the health routes.

500.description: The contract could not be encoded

post.summary: Observe an address without its key
post.description: Observes an address from registration without its key. The entry is watch-only; sending from it answers 422.

400.description: Malformed body, asset tag, or address text

get.description: Every asset tag registered at startup, with its network and metadata. This is the only list of tags the wallet routes accept.

get.summary: Read chain settings and runtime progress
get.description: Returns saved settings, active revisions and reindex progress. Configured RPC URLs are returned for operator editing; environment references are not resolved and authentication headers are omitted.

put.summary: Save chain nodes and requested indexing state
put.description: Persists desired settings before asynchronous verification. Failed candidates keep the active connection. Existing network identities and asset parameters cannot be replaced; networks can be added and nodes edited or reordered.

put.summary: Pause, resume or reindex one network
put.description: Persists requested indexing state. Reindex pauses operations, purges indexed facts, preserves wallet keys and birthdays, then scans again. Poll chain settings for progress.

get.description: Returns bounded in-memory events matching every supplied filter. Use the returned cursor for polling; a changed session requires restarting the cursor.

post.summary: Submit an ordered batch of transfers
post.description: Submits one ordered exact-asset batch of one configured wallet asset. Every asset uses this shared route; no chain-specific transaction route exists. Requests mixing wallet assets are rejected before any transaction is submitted. The asset's chain may group occurrences into one transaction, or reserve consecutive sequence numbers per sender and prepare the whole batch before submitting exact envelopes in request order. Definitely acknowledged transaction IDs are returned only when a non-empty prefix was accepted, and a failed index is returned only when one original occurrence truthfully failed.

400.description: Malformed body, batch size, amount, or destination

422.description: Definite batch failure; transaction_ids is present only for a definitely acknowledged prefix and failed_index only for a truthful item-scoped failure

503.description: Batch unavailable or exact-envelope submission outcome ambiguous; transaction_ids is present only for a definitely acknowledged prefix, failed_index only for a truthful item-scoped failure, and ambiguous_transaction_id only for an unknown outcome

get.summary: List every wallet and watched address
get.description: Every registered wallet and watched address in wallet ID order.

post.summary: Generate a wallet for one configured asset
post.description: Generates a wallet, stores its key in the application registry, then watches it from creation. Keys never leave the server. Retrying creates another wallet.

201.description: Wallet generated and registered for indexing

409.description: Wallet ID or address is already registered

503.description: Wallet generation or registration is unavailable

get.description: The wallet's asset, network, canonical address, and watch-only flag; never its key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The wallet ID a create or watch call returned.

get.summary: Read a wallet's balance in its own asset
get.description: The confirmed indexed total and pending incoming/outgoing amounts in the asset's display units, with the confirmed and pending heights and history completeness. Chain spending rules still apply. A watch-only address reads the same balance without a key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The wallet ID a create or watch call returned.

get.summary: Read one page of a wallet's history
get.description: The wallet's canonical history in the wallet's own asset. `transactions` is confirmed and append-only, so its cursor stays valid however far the checkpoint moves; `pending` carries the transactions above the confirmed line and is populated on the first page only; `completeness` says how much of the history behind the page the index can prove it holds, in the same three words the balance uses.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The wallet ID a create or watch call returned.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

500.description: The next cursor could not be encoded

post.summary: Submit one transfer from a wallet
post.description: Submits one transfer through the wallet's configured asset. Every asset uses this shared route; no chain-specific transaction route exists. A watch-only wallet answers 422. A 202 response means submitted, not confirmed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The wallet ID a create or watch call returned.

422.description: Deterministic rejection, or a watch-only wallet

503.description: Transaction unavailable or exact-envelope submission outcome ambiguous; ambiguous_transaction_id is present only for an unknown outcome

Address.description: A canonical address within its network.

Asset.description: Metadata of the asset an amount is denominated in.

decimals.description: Decimal places between atomic and display units.

id.description: Asset ID within the chain (`native` or a token identifier).

name.description: Display name, when known; always present.

ticker.description: Ticker symbol, when known; always present.

Backfill.description:
The history one network still owes addresses watched from below its
checkpoint, and why the last attempt at it stopped.

It is reported and never gating: a range a pruned node can no longer serve
would otherwise hold `ready` at false for the life of the process while
forward indexing answered every question a client actually asks. The range
is published here, and the reads it weakens say so themselves through their
own `completeness`.

anchor.description:
The highest native block position any of them needs: the network's
confirmed line, which is where an address reading its own past rejoins
the front of the chain. It follows the line until that happens.

oneOf.description:
Why the last attempt stopped short of its budget; null while the range
is merely unfinished. A range that keeps reporting the same failure is
one this node cannot serve: history below `resume` for those addresses
will not arrive until the node can. Always present.

pending.description: How many watched addresses still owe history below their registration.

resume.description: The lowest native block position any of them still needs inspected.

Balance.description:
A wallet's balance in its asset, on both sides of its chain's confirmed
line.

`amount` is the confirmed indexed total. Completeness states whether history
is missing; chain spending rules, such as coinbase maturity, still apply.
The two pending figures describe blocks above the confirmed line: they are
reported apart rather than netted, because "3.0 arriving" and "1.0
leaving" are different facts to a payments operator, and neither is ever
negative. Pending fees are not folded in; a pending transaction's fee is
reported with it in history.

amount.description:
Confirmed indexed amount in exact display units, e.g. `12.5`.
Completeness and chain spending rules apply separately.

completeness.description:
How much of the history behind `amount` the index can prove it holds.
`incomplete` while this address still owes a historical range, and
`overdrawn` when indexed debits exceed known credits.

observed_height.description:
Height of the confirmed line for the saved total; null before a
checkpoint. Always present.

pending_height.description:
Height of the newest block above the confirmed line; null when nothing
is pending. Always present.

pending_incoming.description: Incoming value in blocks above the confirmed line. Never negative.

pending_outgoing.description: Outgoing value in blocks above the confirmed line. Never negative.

transaction_ids.description: Accepted transaction IDs in chain-native submission order.

amount.description: Exact decimal in display units, or `all` to sweep spendable funds.

destination.description: Recipient address text, as the wallet's chain writes it.

Block.description: A block reference: where a transaction was included, or a checkpoint.

oneOf.description: The parent block, when known; always present.

position.description: Chain-native position (a block height or slot).

revision.description: Null when creating a chain; otherwise the last read revision.

Completeness.description:
How much of the history behind an answer the index can prove it holds.

It is a property of the read, not of the wallet, and the balance and the
history page share the vocabulary; opening evidence applies only to balances.

CreateWallet.description: `POST /v1/wallets` body: generate a wallet for one configured asset.

asset.description: The configured asset tag the new wallet holds (`GET /v1/assets`).

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every error response: `message` is always present, the
submission fields only when they are truthfully known.

ambiguous_transaction_id.description:
Canonical ID derived from the exact locally signed envelope. Present only
when its submission outcome remains unknown; its presence produces 503.

failed_index.description:
Zero-based original request index. Present only when one public batch
occurrence truthfully failed.

transaction_ids.description:
Definitely acknowledged transaction IDs before an ordered batch failed.
Present only when that accepted prefix is non-empty.

Event.description: One retained event, with public context and no raw request or provider payload.

Events.description: Polling result. A gap means some records were lost; logs are not an audit ledger.

Fee.description: A transaction fee, always in the chain's native asset.

oneOf.description: Fee payer, when the chain attributes one; always present.

IndexFailure.description:
Why one indexed network is failing: its forward synchronization, or the
historical range it still owes.

attempts.description:
Consecutive attempts that got nowhere: failed passes, and passes whose
backfill was refused.

retryable.description: Whether the same pass can succeed later.

since.description: Unix seconds at which this network entered its current state.

IndexState.description: What one indexed network's synchronization is doing.

Listing.description: One configured asset: its tag, where its wallets live, and what they hold.

asset.description: The tag every wallet route takes (`GET /v1/assets` is the whole list).

network.description: The chain and network this asset's wallets live on.

Movement.description: One value change of the wallet's asset inside a transaction.

oneOf.description: Sender or spent-output owner, when there is one; always present.

kind.description: What kind of value change this is.

oneOf.description: Recipient or created-output owner, when there is one; always present.

Network.description:
The chain and network a wallet, address, or transaction belongs to. It
always ships as one nested object, never as two sibling fields.

NetworkCheckpoint.description: The persisted checkpoint and indexing state of one network.

oneOf.description:
The historical range this network still owes, and why it is stuck;
null when nothing is owed. A network can be `ready` and still report
one: the tip is indexed, and only the addresses named by that range
have history still arriving. Always present.

The last committed block: this network's confirmed line, and the point
`transactions` and `amount` are answered at. Null before the first one.
Always present.

Why forward synchronization is held back. Present exactly when `state`
is `retrying` or `quarantined`. Always present as a field.

The newest block held above the confirmed line; null when nothing is.
Read beside `checkpoint` it shows that a checkpoint below the node's
tip is the chain's confirmation depth rather than lag. Always present.

state.description: What this network's synchronization is doing.

parameters.description: Chain-owned configuration, excluding RPC addresses and credentials.
Chain configuration with an explicit asset tag. Existing parameters are immutable.

origin.description: URL origin for the node card.

url.description: Configured URL for operator editing; environment references remain unresolved.

endpoint.description: URL string or endpoint object (url, headers, bounds). Omit to retain existing credentials.

id.description: Stable identifier; changing URL or order preserves this ID.

Report.description: The memory-only health snapshot of this process.

networks.description: Latest notification for each network; no repository or node calls.

ready.description: Every network settled and at least one ready; false if reporting stopped.

rpc.description: One set of counters per configured RPC endpoint.

Rpc.description: One RPC endpoint's sanitized execution counters.

attempts.description: HTTP executions, including failed attempts hidden by transport retries.

consecutive_failures.description: Failed completions since the last successful completion.

endpoint.description: Zero-based endpoint ordinal in that network's configuration.

last_failure.description: Sanitized failure category; never RPC response text or endpoint credentials.

network.description: Chain and network this client serves.

oneOf.description: In a canonical block above the confirmed line; it may still revert.

confirmations.description: Blocks from inclusion to the newest indexed block, inclusive.

oneOf.description: Committed at or below the confirmed line; it will not revert.

confirmations.description: Blocks from inclusion to the newest indexed block, inclusive.

reason.description: Chain-reported failure reason, when available; always present.

Status.description: Where a history transaction stands relative to its chain's confirmed line.

Transaction.description: One transaction of a wallet's history.

oneOf.description: The fee, when one is attributed; always present.

status.description: Inclusion, confirmation, or failure at a block.

oneOf.description:
The confirmed line the page was read at; null before the first sync.
Always present.

completeness.description:
How much of the history behind this page the index can prove it holds.
`next_cursor` cannot carry it — that speaks about what follows the page,
and a backfill inserts rows *before* it — so a caller paging to the end
mid-backfill reads `incomplete` rather than a complete export.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque cursor of the next page; null when no transaction follows.
Always present.

pending.description:
Transactions in canonical blocks above the confirmed line, oldest
first. They are not in `transactions` because they can still revert,
which would break that list's ordering guarantee. Populated on the
first page only (`cursor` absent), and bounded by the chain's
confirmation depth.

transactions.description:
At most `limit` confirmed transactions; fewer only on the last page.
Append-only: a transaction already returned on a page is never removed
or reordered, so a `next_cursor` stays valid however long it is held.

Transfer.description: `POST /v1/wallets/{id}/transactions` body: one transfer from the path's wallet.

amount.description: Exact decimal in display units, or `all` for the available balance after fees.

destination.description: Recipient address text, as the wallet's chain writes it.

TransferAccepted.description: A submitted, not yet confirmed, transaction.

TransferBatch.description: `POST /v1/transactions` body: an ordered batch of one wallet asset.

transfers.description: Transfers of one configured asset, in execution order.

Wallet.description:
Public wallet fields returned by wallet creation, import, watch, lookup,
and listing.

asset.description: The configured asset tag this wallet holds and sends.

id.description: Wallet ID (a UUIDv7 for wallets and addresses the API registered).

network.description: The chain and network of the wallet's address.

watch_only.description: Observed without a key: history only, no balance or sends.

WatchAddress.description: `POST /v1/addresses` body: observe an address without its key.

address.description: Address text in any form the asset's chain accepts.

asset.description: The configured asset tag whose history to record.

bearerAuth.description: The configured bearer token; health and this document are public.
